repo:cloud#5 · hotlong · session_01Q4EjjPP1zuWBNq3nBXVei9

Ruling text relayed 2026-11-14T03:06Z, on the maintainer's request in seat session `session_01Q4EjjPP1zuWBNq3nBXVei9`: 「server agent 项目读不到 cloud 仓库，请把原文贴到两张卡上」. This card is child 1a of objectstack-ai/cloud#4465 (private repo). Below is the verbatim text of that card's body as last edited at 2026-11-14T03:05Z: the rulings that bear on child 1a (1–5, 9, 10), the environment-side execution terms, the edge paths, and the open facts that name child 1a. Rulings 6 (console invite door), 7 (ADR note) and 8 (direct redirect, carried by objectstack-ai/objectstack#33183) do not bear on this card and are left out. The cloud code paths cited below are in the cloud repo and are given as references, not as files in this repo.

### Rulings (the maintainer, 2026-11-13), verbatim

> 1. **The split.** The production environment is the source of truth for the roster and authorization: people, positions, permission sets, managers, lifecycle. Credentials stay in the cloud: every person is their own cloud account (email verification, password, social login).
> 2. **Who may add people.** An environment administrator who may add users has the same authority as an organization administrator inviting from the console. No separate authorization model.
> 3. **No daily cap** on environment-originated invitations. The basics are kept: each invitation is attributed to the acting administrator, and it is auditable.
> 4. **The invited person's organization role is the ordinary `member`.** The console is not needed, but it is not blocked either. The account is the person's own and can, for example, create a new organization.
> 5. **Deactivation.** Deactivating a plain member in the environment also removes them from the cloud organization. Their environment row and all their history stay. Reactivation re-sends the invitation. Exception: an organization owner or admin cannot be removed from the environment side; that is done in the console.
>
> 9. **Organization owners and admins are environment administrators, projected one way.** The maintainer: 「云端的组织管理员应该就是环境的管理员才合理吧」.
>    - The control plane sends the environment the organization's current owner and admin ids on every change and at kernel build.
>    - The environment grants `admin_full_access` to each linked account, matched by cloud user id, on every entry path. The grant is owned by the Default Organization.
>    - Demotion or removal withdraws only a grant the projection wrote; a grant an environment administrator made stands. Removal also revokes credentials through the existing fan-out.
>    - Nothing flows up: an environment-only administrator stays an organization `member`, and no environment call writes an organization role.
>    - An environment administrator cannot withdraw a projected grant. That is a role change in the console.
>    - 「打开」 enters a non-creator admin as themself. Fact: today every 「打开」 enters as the environment's creator (`routes/environment-lifecycle/sso.ts:318-325`, `auth-proxy-plugin.ts:605-609`), so a non-creator admin has no admin standing of their own on any path.
> 10. **Hosted has no local break-glass admin.** The maintainer chose 「A」.
>    - No hosted environment sets a local password for anyone, and existing owner break-glass passwords are invalidated.
>    - Emergency access is a platform-operator procedure, audited: the platform-admin `disable_platform_sso` / `enable_platform_sso` from cloud#3134, or a one-time recovery link.
>    - Self-hosted deployments keep local admins.
>    - This supersedes cloud#3132's "keep a break-glass local admin" for hosted.
>
> Deferred by the maintainer: 「代理用户先不考虑」. Audited "log in as" is a later item only.
>

### Execution terms for the environment (children 1a / 2b), verbatim

> **Environment (children 1a / 2b):**
> - A platform-admin gate. The environment id comes from the kernel binding.
> - The actor's cloud id comes from the linked `objectstack-cloud` account, never from request input. An admin who entered through the owner handoff is attributed through the handoff's `by` (the handoff signs in as the creator; `handoff-sign-out.ts:9-12`, cloud#2506).
> - Hosted has no local admin (ruling 10). An admin's attribution comes from their own linked cloud account (ruling 9 makes 「打开」 enter as self).
> - A durable outbox with retry (mirror `sys_environment_revocation`), with per-row invitation status in Setup → Users.
> - Deleting or deactivating a pending row cancels its cloud invitation (the email-typo case).
> - An owner or admin 409 refuses the whole deactivation.
> - No database transaction is held across the invite call. The cap calls back into the environment (`GET /_admin/environments/:id/ai-seats`, which fails closed with 503).
> - The pending marker must not read as `env_native`: `set-user-password` admits `env_native` rows (`admin-user-endpoints.ts:1120-1136`), and a row with no `sys_account` reads `env_native` today. Every password door refuses the pending marker.
> - The pending-user door does not depend on the better-auth admin plugin. On Free and Team hosted kernels that plugin mounts only with SCIM (`auth-manager-plugin-list.ts:211`; `admin/import-users` answers 501 there, `auth-plugin.ts:4604`). Mounting it on hosted would also expose impersonate and ban, which needs its own ruling.

### Edge paths the children must cover, verbatim

> - **Console-side removal or role change** of a person the environment lists as active: the environment row stays active but cannot sign in. The roster shows that state.
> - **A person invited directly from the console** has no pending row and arrives by JIT, as today.
> - **Adding an email that already has an environment row:** decide in child 1a whether that is a refusal or an update.
> - **Reactivation, or a CSV row, at the developer cap** is refused with 403 `DEVELOPER_ORGANIZATION_MEMBER_LIMIT_REACHED`. This is shown per row, and a CSV import reports partial failures row by row.
> - **A pending row that never accepts:** it stays pending, can be re-sent, and can be deleted, which cancels the invitation.

### Open facts naming child 1a, verbatim

> - Does `admin/ban-user` (today's deactivation) answer on a Free hosted kernel? If not, child 1a needs its own deactivation door.

### Rulings recorded after the body (comment 6870693029 on cloud#4465)

> d-2 应急入口不考虑 d-3 同意

For this card: D-3 means stored local password hashes on hosted are refused, not deleted, so every password door refuses rather than clears. D-2 means no one-time recovery link is built; ruling 10's emergency access is not extended here.
